title: Short Stuff: The SS Ourang Medang
summary: Short Stuff episode on the SS Orang Medang (also spelled Orangmudan in the transcript), a purported Dutch freighter found drifting as a ghost ship with its crew apparently dead in the Straits of Malacca, which exploded or sank after an American ship, the Silver Star, tried to tow it. The hosts explain the story is likely a fabrication traced to a single writer, Silvio Shirley, who first published it in 1940 (per researcher Estelle Hargraves), and that the 1948 Dutch Indonesian newspaper version added a survivor and illicit-cargo explanation. They also discuss the ship's pop culture influence, including a 2019 horror video game "The Quarry"-style reference to "The Man of Medan" and the influence on True Detective: Night Country, and note that their source was a HowStuffWorks article.

segments.title: Opening banter and Man of Medan game
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the ghost ship topic and discuss the 2019 horror game The Man of Medan, named after the English translation of the ship's name.

segments.title: The SOS and the ghost ship account
segments.summary: The hosts recount the Dutch freighter's garbled SOS message about dead officers and crew, and the Silver Star's arrival to find the ship apparently abandoned.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: A short break is taken before the detailed account of the boarding.

segments.title: Boarding the ship and the crew's fate
segments.summary: A sailor boards the silent ship and finds the crew and a dog frozen in fearful poses; the hosts compare it to True Detective: Night Country, then the tow attempt and the ship's explosion and sinking.

segments.title: Is the story real? Hoax and origins
segments.summary: The hosts argue the ship was likely fabricated, noting no shipping records or survivors and varying details. Researcher Estelle Hargraves traced the story's origin to a 1940 article by Silvio Shirley, first published before the supposed event.

segments.title: 1948 newspaper version and illicit cargo theory
segments.summary: The 1948 Dutch Indonesian newspaper Der Locomotief version adds a survivor found by a missionary and an illicit cargo explanation. The hosts question whether the sources can be trusted given deepfake concerns.

segments.title: Sources and closing remarks
segments.summary: The hosts note the episode was based on a HowStuffWorks article and that another article referenced it, then close the episode.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Chuck gives the standard iHeartRadio production credit and podcast promotion.
